issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE lacks the `i` flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it, breaking case-insensitivity symmetry for keyframe selectors.
issues.detail: CSS treats `from`/`to` case-insensitively, and HAS_KEYWORD reflects that with the `i` flag. HAS_PERCENTAGE does not match the same contract, which strengthens the precondition asymmetrically and risks silently dropping legitimate rules like `FROM { ... }`. Apply the flag uniformly or document why percentage tokens don't need it.

issues.description: Fast-path presence regexes can over-match inside comments, var() fallbacks, or attribute selectors without documented over-approximation contract.
issues.detail: `\burl\(`, `\b(?:100|...|900)\b`, and `:not(` will match inside comments, `var(--font-700)`, or `[data-x=":not("]`. This is safe only because matches widen to the slow path, but the over-approximation invariant is implicit. Add a brief spec comment per regex stating the fast-reject contract.

issues.description: `selectorRegex = /./` sentinel for "match everything" is an abstraction leak and bad taste.
issues.detail: Using a match-anything regex to mean "no filter" forces the caller to know walkRules' filter semantics. Cleaner to branch: call `walkRules(cb)` when no filter is needed and `walkRules(regex, cb)` otherwise. Same machine code, clearer intent for the next maintainer.

issues.description: Fast-reject pattern repeated across six rules with no shared abstraction or named contract.
issues.detail: Each rule reinvents "compile a presence regex, bail early if absent." Without naming this idiom (e.g., `quickReject(value, primary)`) or documenting it once, future contributors won't know the fast-path must over-approximate the slow-path. Establish the convention before it ossifies across more rules.

issues.description: import-notation `url` branch inverts filter polarity vs sibling rules without explanatory comment.
issues.detail: For `primary === 'url'`, the code returns when `url(` IS present — opposite from other rules. This is correct (violation = string form when url expected), but the asymmetry invites a future maintainer to "fix" it. A one-line comment stating the precondition each branch filters for would prevent regression.

issues.description: Case-sensitivity asymmetry between HAS_NAMED and HAS_NUMERIC in font-weight-notation is undocumented.
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive while HAS_NUMERIC is case-sensitive. For numeric weights this is harmless, but the inconsistency deserves a one-line comment so the next reader doesn't assume it's a bug. Pick one stance and document it.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-MINOR-WORK: the PR is a sound performance optimization adding cheap presence-check prefilters before expensive parser walks across six notation rules. The main concrete bug is the HAS_PERCENTAGE / HAS_KEYWORD case-flag asymmetry in keyframe-selector-notation, which violates the fast-reject contract. Taste issues include the `/./` sentinel, undocumented over-approximation invariants, and inverted filter polarity in import-notation. Naming and documenting the fast-reject pattern before it spreads further is the panel's strongest structural recommendation.
